items.summaryJa: 岡山理科大学サッカー部が生成AI「Gemini」を活用した教育・チーム運営の取り組みが、Google Gemini公式noteの前編・後編およびGoogle Japan公式Xで紹介されました。 学生自身が課題を言語化し考える力を育む「思考のパートナー」としてGeminiを活用し、選手個人の活用からチーム運営へと展開、学外活動の運営やデータ分析、広報など多方面で課題解決に取り組んでいます。 今後も教員と学生の協働だけでなく、学生同士が生成AIを活用する取り組みを広げ、AIを活用し自ら考え判断し行動できる人材の育成を目指すとのことです。

items.summaryJa: N高グループの生徒会役員とデジタル委員会は、Googleの生成AI「Gemini」を活用した実践型イベント『Gemini-1グランプリ』を開催し、2025年7月〜2026年2月の期間に計6回実施、最終応募総数は3,411件となりました。評価はプロンプト設計やアウトプットの質だけでなく、意図や試行錯誤の過程、活用方法の独自性、課題への論理的アプローチを重視しました。今後は継続的なAI活用企画の実施や学園内でのAI活用文化の普及を目指し、参加しやすい設計と生徒主体の運営を継続します。

items.summaryJa: 西大和学園高校で約250名の1年生を対象に、Google Geminiを使って生成AIの活用方法と注意点を学ぶワークショップが実施された。DXハイスクール事業採択を受け、基礎を重視した内容で、体験と講義を組み合わせ、AIリテラシーやプロンプトデザインなどの基礎3層を土台とする教育フレームワークを用いた。生徒は質問の工夫や逆翻訳、要約演習を通じてAIの回答を鵜呑みにせず検証する体験を行い、AI活用と自分で考える力の両立の重要性を理解した。

items.summaryJa: マイクロソフトはRustを“Tier-1言語”として位置付け、C++・C#・TypeScriptと同様に手厚くサポートする方針を示した。Rustは所有権・借用によるメモリ安全性とC++並みの高速性を特徴とし、同社はWindowsカーネルやフォント解析、Chromiumの画像デコーダーなどで採用を進めている。特に「rustc_codegen_utc」バックエンドの投資により、Windowsのツールチェーン・ABIとの互換性向上やC++との相互運用を実現し、2026年初頭には製品レベルでの利用が見込まれている。

items.titleJa: AppleやGoogleら3社、空間オーディオにまつわる特許を保有する米企業から訴えられる - INTERNET Watch
items.summaryJa: 空間オーディオの特許を保有する米企業BoomCloud 360が、Apple・Google・Samsungの3社を訴えた。ITCが正式調査を開始したが、直ちに不正行為や特許侵害を確定するものではなく、同社は自社技術を守る目的で提訴したという。もし同社の主張が認められれば、米国での販売が一部または全て禁止される可能性があり、日本での販売にも影響が及ぶ可能性がある。なお3社はそれぞれ確認判決訴訟を提起しており、結論は比較的短期間で判明する見通し。

items.title: Anthropic says its model Claude is helping to build the next version of itself - ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
items.summary: Anthropic says its model Claude is helping to build the next version of itself    ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
items.titleJa: Anthropic says its model Claude is helping to build the next version of itself - ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
items.summaryJa: Anthropicは、自社のAI Claudeが次世代のより知的なモデルの開発を支援していると発表した。Claudeは同社のモデル開発の約26%を担い、高レベルの指示から“ほぼ端末作業を完結”できるとされるが、完全 autonomousにはまだ至っていない。研究開発の約90%はClaudeと協働して行われ、モデルが人の指示の下で大きな作業を進められると説明されている。

items.summaryJa: Googleはスマートホーム基盤のGoogle Homeを、外部AIエージェントから制御可能にする新規格「Home MCP」を早期アクセス開始した。外部AIエージェントはModel Context Protocolを介して照明やサーモスタット、カメラなどを読み取り・操作でき、自然言語指示で横断的な映像要約やイベント履歴解析、カスタムダッシュボードの作成が可能になる。安全対策として高リスク操作は不可で、顔認識データを使う場合は管理者の同意とアクセス権限の取り消しが可能となっている。

items.summaryJa: KDDIはGoogle Cloudの「Gemini Enterprise」を活用した「KDDI AIエージェント開発支援」の提供を開始し、企業のAIエージェント導入を支援する。閉域網サービスやデータ整備、ELYZAによる高度な開発支援を組み合わせ、機密情報の取り扱いを安全に行いながら業務プロセスの自動化と生産性向上を目指す。データ整備はフライウィールが担当し、KDDIのファースト/セカンドパーティデータやSpeedaの経済情報と組み合わせてAI活用を高度化する。

items.summaryJa: Google Geminiとnoteのコラボ企画「#AIとできたこと」で、AIを活用して前に進んだ体験を募集します。募集期間は2026年9月18日から10月18日で、応募はnoteのアカウントとGoogle Gemini公式アカウントのフォロー、そしてハッシュタグ「#AIとできたこと」を付けた投稿が条件です。受賞はグランプリ1名（10万円分ギフトカード）ほか、Google Gemini賞などがあり、受賞作品にはGoogle AI Proプランの3ヶ月無料特典が提供されます。

items.summaryJa: Googleは実験的AIエージェント「CC」をアップデートし、個人だけでなく家族・世帯向けに拡張すると発表した。CCは専用アカウントを持ち、最大6人で共有できるようになり、家族の予定・タスクの管理や文書作成支援、買い物リスト作成などを自動化する機能を提供する。現在は米国の18歳以上の個人ユーザー向けで日本は対象外だが、将来的にこうした家族向け機能の利用を検討している。

items.title: California's new partnership with Anthropic sparks questions about security and state data - KCRA
items.summary: California's new partnership with Anthropic sparks questions about security and state data    KCRA
items.titleJa: California's new partnership with Anthropic sparks questions about security and state data - KCRA
items.summaryJa: 州政府とAnthropicの新たな協力関係により、AnthropicのチャットボットClaudeを50%割引で利用できるほか、無料の研修と技術サポートが提供されることになった。費用は「ゼロドル契約」とされ、各機関が個別に料金を設定・支払う形で、月額1人あたり10ドルの基本料金と、テキストの処理量に応じた料金が発生する見込みだが、総費用は不明だ。データの安全性については、州データを訓練に使わない条項などがある一方で、機密性の高い情報の扱いには依然として懸念があり、技術的・法的な完全性は保証されないとの見方もある。

items.titleJa: Microsoft Word用ChatGPTアドインがリリース
items.summaryJa: OpenAIは2026年9月17日、Microsoft Wordに対応したChatGPTアドインを発表した。Wordのサイドパネルから起動して、下書き作成、文書の編集・書式設定、校正、難解な段落の整理などを、Wordを離れずに依頼できるようになり、OutlookやSharePoint、Google Workspace、Dropboxなどの連携アプリも活用できる。Word対応アドインはバージョン2.0.0.1以降で、Microsoft Marketplaceから入手可能。今回の発表に伴い、BusinessおよびEnterpriseプランのユーザーには9月17日〜30日の間、Word上でのGPT-5.6 Solの無料プレビューが提供される。

items.title: 「Claude Code」のプロジェクト機能が向上--AIが作業全体を統括 - ZDNET Japan
items.summary: 「Claude Code」のプロジェクト機能が向上--AIが作業全体を統括    ZDNET Japan
items.titleJa: 「Claude Code」のプロジェクト機能が向上--AIが作業全体を統括 - ZDNET Japan
items.summaryJa: Anthropicは Claude Code のプロジェクト機能を再設計し、複数のエージェントを協調させるオーケストレーション機能と、スレッドごとに独自ブランチを割り当てるクラウドセッションを新設した。新機能により、エージェント間の作業割り当てや出力の検証、最終成果物の組み立てを Claude が自動的に統括するほか、スレッド間で共有メモリーを用いた情報追加・取得が可能になり、複雑なプロンプト設計の必要性が軽減されるという。現時点ではクラウド上の機能で、近くローカル環境でも動作するようになる予定だが、ローカル環境向けツールの提供時期は未定である。

items.title: Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs - Anthropic
items.summary: Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs    Anthropic
items.titleJa: Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs - Anthropic
items.summaryJa: AIは自らの開発を加速させる動きを示しており、AnthropicはAIがAI開発をどれだけ担うか、AIによる監督と介入の実効性、そして開発を支える資源を測る指標を報告しています。本文では、Claudeが Anthropic の AI R&D の作業のうちAIが主導・協働する割合や、オンライン・オフライン監視を通じた監督の実情、約30,000名規模のエージェントの運用状況と監視指標を提示しています。これらの指標は、外部からの検証や第三者評価を受けつつ、前線ラボの開発ペースを透明にすることを目的としています。

items.title: 英チャールズ国王、AI大手トップらに「実存的な危険」を警告 NVIDIAやOpenAI、Anthropicが参加 - ITmedia

items.summaryJa: チャールズ国王は英国のAIサミットで、AIの発展は「興味深くもあり、同時に深く憂慮すべきもの」だと指摘し、技術が悪用される実存的リスクを防ぐための十分な制御手段が必要だと訴えた。NVIDIAやGoogle DeepMind、OpenAI、Anthropicの代表を含む約30人規模の参加者は、安全性を最優先にした取り組みと、技術を人類や社会に奉仕させることの重要性を共有した。出席者の中にはNVIDIAのジェンスン・フアンCEOやAnthropicのティノ・クエヤル氏、DeepMindのデミス・ハサビス氏らが含まれた。

items.title: Anthropic shares 3 metrics to help AI companies monitor pace of development - CNBC

items.titleJa: Anthropic shares 3 metrics to help AI companies monitor pace of development - CNBC
items.summaryJa: Anthropicは、AI企業が開発の pace を把握できる3つの新指標を公表した。指標は、AI主導の研究開発、AIエージェントの監視と介入、全計算資源の配分の3点で構成され、それぞれの測定方法も共有する。これらは、モデル能力の評価と併せて、外部が開発の速度を判断する出発点となることを意図している。

items.title: Sub-second artifact deployments are now supported in Vercel CLI
items.summary: You and your agents can now deploy static artifacts to Vercel in under one second through Vercel CLI. Run vercel deploy to share a prototype, publish an HTML report, or preview a page created by your coding agent. Vercel automatically detects eligible deployments, and valid artifacts will skip the build step, immediately returning a live URL. Instant deployments support directories with: Up to 10 HTML or Markdown files A total size of 5 MB or less Supported file extension include .html , .htm , and .md. Update to Vercel CLI version 59.16.0 or later to get started, and run vercel deploy --help for all available options. Read more

items.title: Run Terminal-Bench and other Harbor evals on Vercel Sandbox
items.summary: You can now run Harbor evals on Vercel Sandbox. Harbor is the open-source harness behind Terminal-Bench , whose registry includes many other benchmarks such as SWE-bench, tau3-bench and OSWorld. Pass --env vercel to harbor run and each trial executes in its own isolated Firecracker microVM, so you can parallelize far beyond what your local machine is capable of. A task's network policy is enforced at the sandbox firewall, outside the VM. Optional credential injection attaches secrets to matching outbound requests at that firewall, so they never enter the sandbox. Paired with AI Gateway , one AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY reaches hundreds of models from multiple providers, and benchmarking another model is the same command with a different --model : Swap --model to vercel_ai_gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna to run the same benchmark against an OpenAI model. Requires Harbor 0.22.0 or later. Follow the step-by-step guide for setup, configuration, and troubleshooting. Learn more in the Sandbox documentation . Read more

items.title: Open-weight models take 56% of token volume, Astra doubles Fable 5.1 spend
items.summary: AI Gateway Production Index — September 2026 Every month, AI Gateway routes tens of trillions of tokens between production applications and AI labs. That traffic gives us a view of what AI usage actually looks like in today's enterprise, and we publish it here monthly. See the Production Index reports from June , July , and August . September 2026 summary The September index reports on AI Gateway data collected through August 2026. Open-weight models ran the majority of gateway tokens for the first time, up from 7% in December to 56% in August. The average token costs less than half what it did five months ago. Price per token fell 23.2% in August, the third straight monthly drop, and the median team paid 7.6% less. Fable 5, Anthropic's most capable model, lost two-thirds of its share of gateway spend in one month. Opus 5, at half the price, tripled its share. Anthropic kept 64% of all spend. Gemini 3 Flash has lost 95% of its share of gateway tokens since May, and more than three-quarters of the volume it lost went to models from other labs. Special report: OpenAI launches Astra on September 3 GPT-6 Astra took a third of OpenAI's spend within two days of launch and twice Fable 5.1's share of gateway spend. Introduced two days apart at the same price, Astra took 7.7% of all gateway spend in its first twelve days, while Fable 5.1 took 3.7%. Open-weight models take a majority of token volume for the first time In August, open-weight models ran 56% of all tokens on AI Gateway, marking the first month they took the majority of volume. In December 2025, they processed fewer than one in ten tokens, and only eight months later, they ran more token volume than all closed-weight models combined. Though the frontier kept the majority of spend, open-weight dollar share is accelerating. As open-weight models become more capable, customers are moving more production workloads over to them. Growth in open-weight model adoption helped push the average price per token across the gateway down 23.2% in August, its third consecutive monthly drop and the steepest since April. Among teams running more than ten million tokens in both months, the median team paid 7.6% less per token, more than double July's 2.9% decline. Teams can now get more inference from the same budget and reserve frontier models only for the tasks that justify the premium. Frontier plateaus as Fable spend goes to Opus 5 Production workloads that justify a frontier model don't always need the most expensive one. They need one that’s good enough. Fable is the most capable model Anthropic sells. Opus is the tier below it and costs roughly half of Fable’s price per token. When the US export control on Fable 5 was lifted and its access restored on July 1, its gateway spend share surged to 13.2%. At the end of that same month, Opus 5 came online. In August, Fable 5’s share of gateway spend fell to 4.9%, and Opus 5's share rose to 22.5%. Nine in ten of the teams that ran Fable cut their usage, and more of them moved their workloads to Opus 5 than any other model. Fable’s extra capability wasn’t worth double the price. Teams left Fable, Anthropic's most expensive and capable model, but the lab retained the lion’s share of gateway spend because those workloads stepped down to Opus 5, not a different lab. Anthropic has taken at least 61 cents of every dollar spent through AI Gateway every month since December, and 64 cents in August. Its models have held the top two spots by spend every month since December, even as the models in those spots changed. Customer loyalty follows the model profile, not the lab Lab loyalty doesn’t follow brand, it follows model profile, and consistency wins. When a new model preserves what users valued in its predecessor, the lab retains its customers. When it doesn’t, those customers fill the need through other providers. When Claude Opus 5 launched, it gained almost twice what Fable lost, because it handled the same workloads at half the price. And within five days of Z.ai launching GLM-5.3-Flash, it was running three times GLM-5.2's daily volume. Google struggled to retain customers with its new models. Because the new offerings didn’t provide a relative advantage on capability or price, a majority of Gemini 3 Flash’s workloads moved to OpenAI, Anthropic, and DeepSeek. About half of the volume that left Gemini 3 Flash went to cheaper models, led by GPT-5.6 Luna, which costs less than half as much per token. Most of the other half went to higher-priced models, led by Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5, which cost roughly nine and three times as much as Gemini 3 Flash, respectively. The flight to better-fit models meant that over the same period, Google’s share of gateway token volume fell from 30% to 5%, with Gemini 3 Flash accounting for 22 of the 25 percentage points lost. Special report: Astra took a third of OpenAI spend within 48 hours and outpaced Fable 5.1 two to one at launch GPT-6 Astra launched on the AI Gateway on September 3 at the same price as Fable 5.1 and two and a half times the price of GPT-5.6 Sol. Two days later, it accounted for one in every three dollars spent on OpenAI models through the gateway. Its share of spend has held, hovering between 28% and 39% since. Within OpenAI’s model lineup, Astra and Sol processed 27% of OpenAI’s tokens but accounted for 71% of its spending from September 4 through 16. Luna and Nano processed more than twice as many tokens for about one-ninth as much spending. Anthropic launched Fable 5.1 on September 1, two days before Astra. Over each model's first twelve days on the gateway, Astra took 7.7% of all gateway spend, more than twice Fable 5.1's share of 3.7%, and was used by twice as many teams. OpenAI’s cheaper models carry its volume, while Astra’s early lead over Fable shows it can also attract teams at the highest price point. Together, they let OpenAI compete with other frontier labs for both scale and premium spend. Stay tuned for more in next month's report. Also in August’s data Google's Nano Banana took the lead in image spend for the first time , at 50% to GPT Image's 44%, even as GPT Image took back the lead in images generated, 46% to 39%. Google's Veo rose to second in video spend, at 20%, up from 15% in July. Seedance remained in first on both videos generated and video spend. The share of videos generated by xAI’s Grok Imagine has more than halved since June, from 42% to 31% to 19%. items.title: How Delphi ships 100 times a day with its Python backend on Vercel
items.summary: Delphi on Vercel 10 engineers with no dedicated infrastructure role Everyone ships code, including product and design 100+ production deploys a day behind feature flags Delphi builds digital minds. They capture what someone has written, recorded, and taught, so anyone can tap that expertise on demand. Delphi is “a destination where you can find and interact with interesting minds,” says founding engineer Spencer Schoeben. Nobody has built a digital mind network before, so Delphi figures out what to build by shipping features and watching how people use them. That only works if the product is fast to change. "If we are going to win, we need to have an excellent developer and agentic experience," Spencer says. "Otherwise, we could not adapt to how fast our user’s demands change." Delphi's frontend had run on Vercel since day one. "The frontend has always been easy," Spencer says, "but the backend was a nightmare." Six months ago, the team rebuilt its Python backend on Vercel as well. Today the whole team ships to production 100+ times a day. Building a Python backend that's easy to work on The backend slowed every change Delphi's backend previously ran on AWS, with ECS, Docker Desktop, and local databases. In the earliest days, the setup worked because the team was small and much of the context lived in people’s heads. As Delphi grew, that made onboarding slower than the team wanted: getting a new engineer to their first deploy took a full day of environment setup. Delphi could have fixed that without leaving AWS. But fixing it properly would have meant designing and owning the infrastructure themselves, and the team didn't want to own infrastructure at all. "That is not our current goal as a company," Spencer says. After moving the backend to Vercel, new engineers could get to production much faster, with the same deploy workflow the rest of the team used every day. Workflows and Queues made the move possible When Delphi was founded, Vercel Workflows and Vercel Queues didn't exist. Without them, Spencer says, the move would have been much harder, if possible at all. Delphi's backend depends on long-running work and queued background jobs. Digital minds need durable agents that generate content ahead of time, plus ingestion that turns a person's books and talks into a knowledge graph. Workflows handles the long-running work and Queues handle the background jobs. Neither requires setup. A developer writes the workflow or the queue handler as a function in the codebase, and Vercel provisions what's needed to run it on deploy. 100+ deploys a day, straight to production Moving the backend to Vercel let Delphi stop treating backend changes as heavyweight releases and ship them as everyday product work. The team used to deploy to staging, then production. Now it skips the middle step, shipping 100+ times a day behind feature flags and running A/B tests instead of batching changes into a release. Vercel Agent's anomaly detection watches production at that pace, flagging when something is misbehaving and why. Before, Spencer says, they often would not have known. Moving fast has helped clear a backlog of small experiments that never used to make the priority list. Many of those experiments test how to turn a visitor into an owner, someone who arrives to talk to a mind and leaves having started their own. Shipping isn't limited to engineers, either. Delphi's CPO and its growth teams build and deploy dashboards, prototypes, and experiments themselves, which Spencer says wouldn't have happened on the old setup. Infrastructure built for agents and engineers Preview deployments are how agents check their work Delphi's engineers hand problems to cloud agents, with very little development happening locally. The preview deployment is where they first see what the agent built. Vercel preview deployments give every push its own live URL, so anyone can check the result from a phone or a Slack thread without pulling the branch. When an agent fails, it's usually because it couldn't get at the information it needed. Vercel exposes the data and controls agents need through the SDK, MCP, and CLI, so an agent can read logs, inspect a deployment, or change an environment variable through whichever it's using. For Delphi, agents are now the main users of those tools, so the platform has to be as easy for them as it is for people. An internal agent on Sandbox for customer success Delphi's own agents run on Vercel as well. One of them, an internal agent on Vercel Sandbox , simplifies working with the company's codebase. The customer success team uses Slack to ask it about reported issues, find the problem, and hand an engineer a root cause and a proposed fix. Edge cases used to fall through the cracks. "Before, we either couldn't get to everything, or we had to spend way more time than we had available," Spencer says. "Now we have an agent they can just ask in Slack." Vercel Sandbox gives the agent an isolated environment with a file system, where it can check out the codebase, run it, and pull in whatever data a question needs. The agent itself is built with eve, Vercel's agent framework. Delphi's first version ran on a hosted agent platform and could only use the integrations that platform offered. In eve, tools are code Delphi writes, so when a question needs one that doesn't exist, the team adds it. AI Gateway picks the model for each mind Delphi's chat traffic runs through AI Gateway. Every digital mind is different, and some come out better on one model than another, so Delphi picks the model for each customer and adjusts as its own evals change. When a new model ships, open-source or otherwise, Delphi can route to it the same day. Gateway also handles failover. Before, Delphi worked directly with a model provider to line up fallback capacity on other clouds, and it was hard. "With AI Gateway, we always know that we're going to get the fallbacks if they exist," Spencer says. What's next Delphi's first chapter was training digital minds and letting people chat with them. Now it is building the interface beyond chat. Spencer describes a search page where you bring a question, get perspectives from several minds at once, and have the page adapt to who you are. That work runs as long-running agents on Workflows, with AI Gateway supplying whichever model each experiment calls for. About Delphi : Delphi is a platform that turns a person's knowledge, thinking, and voice into a digital mind others can talk to. Anyone can create their own Delphi to make their expertise discoverable and accessible, part of a network of minds people can seek out, learn from, and converse with. Read more

items.title: AI SDK harness layer now supports native subscription authentication
items.summary: The AI SDK harness layer now supports authenticating harnesses through their native subscriptions, where the underlying harness supports them. The harness layer runs different coding agents through the same HarnessAgent interface, so you can switch agents without changing your application code. No code changes or new settings are required. The direct authentication mode uses explicit provider environment credentials when they are present, and otherwise a native subscription found on the host. The default auto mode does the same when no AI Gateway credentials are set. The ai-gateway mode never reads native subscriptions. Native subscription credentials stay on the host. Just like with API keys, credentials are resolved at the host boundary. OAuth access tokens are refreshed there as needed. Where the sandbox supports it, the harness receives placeholder credentials and the real token is injected into outbound requests on the host. Native subscriptions work across harness adapters wherever the harness itself supports subscription login. These include Claude Code, Cline, Codex, Cursor, fx, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, OpenCode, and Pi. Read the harness documentation to learn more. Read more
